title: Mapping scientific literature with large language models and topic modeling
subcategory: science mapping with recursive clustering and LLM labelling
task: Mapping a journal's engineering literature into interpretable topics and cross-topic links
problem: Keyword systems and bag-of-words topic models struggle to capture the fragmented, interdisciplinary structure of modern science.
architecture: Abstracts embedded with text-embedding-3-small and clustered by K-means; GPT-4o-mini writes a label and description per cluster and re-classifies every abstract five times (3-of-5 consensus); clusters with agreement >= 0.60 are kept and the rest re-clustered recursively; a second full-text pass assigns secondary topics; a bipartite network links primary and secondary topics.

datasets.name: PNAS
datasets.details: engineering-related articles over 20 years; 1,493 validated research articles

key_results: Highest topic diversity (0.909) and lowest Jaccard overlap (6.15E-03) vs BERTopic 0.765 and 2.90E-02; MALLET LDA has the best C_V (0.540 vs 0.446).
Manual validation accuracy 75.9% on a 20% sample (303 abstracts); 16 topics plus an 'Other' category covering 9.8% of abstracts.
strengths: Consensus re-classification reduces LLM stochasticity; an 'Other' category flags emerging or noisy content.

limitations.text: The number of clusters per recursion step must be fixed or chosen heuristically.
Automated coherence metrics may not align with human judgement.
Coherence (C_V, UMass) is lower than several classical baselines.
